messages:
maya: Hey team — our CI deploy job started failing right after the service account tokens were rotated last night. Jenkins `deploy-master` now gets a 401 from the API. Request log shows 'invalid_scope' in the body. Anyone familiar with this pattern?

samir: can you paste the exact error and a curl repro? quick checks: which SA is the pipeline using (ci-deploy?) and are we talking long-lived API keys or short-lived OIDC tokens?

maya: using `ci-deploy` service-account via the old CI bot user. This was working until the token rotation window (we rolled secrets at ~00:15 UTC). here's the curl we used in the job:

```bash
TOKEN=$CI_TOKEN
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.run/v1/deploy
```

Response:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{'error':'unauthorized', 'detail':'token_scope_missing'}
```

maya: stack trace in the job shows the call to /v1/deploy returns permission denied, but other endpoints (e.g., /v1/status) still work.

jordan: interesting — that suggests the token is valid but missing the `deploy:write` scope. When the rotation ran did the SA get a new role mapping? We updated the token lifetimes last week to favor short-lived OIDC tokens for CI. If the CI is still presenting a long-lived key we might be hitting a mismatch in accepted token types/scopes.

lia: I saw the audit log: rotation script created a new token for `ci-deploy` but the script used the default scopes (read-only) instead of the `deploy` scope because the --scopes flag was omitted. Bot operator error. Audit id: audit-20240315-78f.

maya: oof. that explains why /v1/status works (read) and /v1/deploy fails (write). What do we recommend as the fix? Re-create token with deploy scope?

samir: short term: create a replacement token with correct scopes and update Jenkins creds. Example command (ops CLI):

```bash
redwoodctl sa token create --sa ci-deploy --scopes deploy:write,config:read --ttl 30d --output token.txt
# then update CI credential with token.txt contents
```

samir: long term we should stop using long-lived static tokens in CI. Switch to workload identity / OIDC federation so Jenkins requests short-lived tokens with requested scopes. Also add an assertion in the rotation script to validate scopes post-create.

maya: quick repro steps I'm going to run on staging: 1) rotate token with no scopes, 2) run `deploy-master` job, 3) observe 401 on deploy. I can post the exact logs.

ops-bot: Jenkins pipeline #4217 failed: stage=deploy, exit=1, job=deploy-master, cause=unauthorized (audit-20240315-78f).

maya: repro confirmed on staging. Logs: `token_scope_missing` for /v1/deploy.

jordan: FYI for least-privilege, we should split `ci-deploy` into two service accounts: `ci-deploy-trigger` (only start jobs) and `ci-deploy-exec` (write deploys, limited TTL). That reduces blast radius if a token leaks.

lia: opened a tiny patch to the rotation script to require --scopes and to run `redwoodctl sa token inspect` after creation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412

samir: made a temporary token with the right scopes and applied to Jenkins; doing a manual run now.

maya: manual run succeeded, deploy step passed. Green. :tada:

maya: follow-ups: 1) add a runbook entry under support/runbooks/ci-tokens.md for how to rotate and validate CI tokens, 2) schedule a migration to OIDC federation for Jenkins (ops ticket created), 3) consider lowering default token TTL for SA tokens created by the rotation script.

jordan: also add a linter check in the rotation script CI that rejects token creation without explicit scopes.

lia: adding the runbook now and linking the PR. I'll also add an alert rule that triggers if `token_scope_missing` errors spike across CI pipelines.

maya: thanks all — leaving the temp token expiring in 30d, will follow up once we migrate the pipeline to OIDC.

samir: note for support: if you see 401s with `token_scope_missing`, check audit logs for `sa token create` events around the rotate time, inspect token scopes with `redwoodctl sa token inspect <token_id>`, and rotate with --scopes if needed.

ops-bot: ticket SUP-2387 created: 'CI pipelines failing after SA rotation (missing scopes)'. Assigned to maya, lia.

maya: marking this thread resolved for now, will reopen if anything else pops up.
